title: Bounded finite free model of the derived dual on an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $U\subseteq X$ an affine open. Let $F$ be a bounded complex of finite free $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-pc-derived-category]. There is a bounded finite free complex $D$ on $U$ and an isomorphism $Q(D)\cong R\mathcal Hom(Q(F),(\mathcal O_X[0])|_U)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], where $\mathcal O_X[0]$ is the actual unit of the shared derived tensor structure [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure].

source.place: Tag 08DQ, proof of lemma-dual-perfect-complex; Tag 08DM, lemma-RHom-strictly-perfect

proof.text: Construct D as homComplex(F,O_U[0]). Its specified degree-n product projections have zero factors at p other than -n, since O_U[0] vanishes in degree p+n and internal Hom is additive in its second variable. Lift the identity at the sole remaining factor and zero at the others to construct the inverse projection. Product hom-ext proves its two inverse identities. Thus D^n is Hom(F^(-n),O_U), as proved in the private helper homComplex_dual_term_iso.

If F is bounded in [a,b], then D is bounded in [-b,-a], since Hom from zero is zero. Transport the finite free isomorphism for F^(-n) contravariantly under Hom(-,O_U) and apply the proved source-library homObjFreeUnitIso. This proves finite freeness in degree n. Both assertions are proved in homComplex_dual_bounded_finiteFree.

The shared derived unit is Qh of the homotopy class of O_X[0]. quotientCompQhIso identifies it with Q(O_X[0]). Restrict this isomorphism, use mapDerivedCategoryFactors, then singleMapHomologicalComplex. Restriction of the underived unit is definitionally the localized unit. This gives the proved restricted_derived_unit_iso without a monoidal restriction assumption.

Make F strictly perfect using each free isomorphism and its inverse as retraction maps. Apply the strictly perfect ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison to F and O_U[0]. Apply RHom in its second variable to the inverse of the restricted-unit isomorphism and compose to obtain the displayed comparison.

theorem exists_bounded_finiteFree_derived_dual_model
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) [IsAffine U.toScheme]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [hU : HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (F : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (F.X n))
    (hfree : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (F.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U) (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))) :
    ∃ D : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ,
      (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (D.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (D.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free
        (R := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U) (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))) ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj D ≅
        (@derivedInternalHom.{u, w} (Over U) _
          ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace).over U)
          (X.toRingedSpace.sheaf.over U) hU).obj
          (op ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := SheafOfModules.{u}
              ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))).obj F),
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
              (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
                (𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory X))))
